samples.summary: New shared helper `resolveCheckNames` has no test at all
samples.evidence: `resolveCheckNames(args, {read, log})` is added in prior-findings.mjs:132 and is the single input resolver for BOTH new CLIs (fix-brief.mjs:34, fix-eligible.mjs:37). Its documented contract is load-bearing: `--checks` must win over `--lenses`, and an unreadable manifest must return `[]` (which callers turn into exit 2 rather than "no panel ran", i.e. an accidental eligibility). Grepping the whole repo for `resolveCheckNames` returns only the definition and the two imports — no test file references it, and prior-findings.test.mjs contains no case for it. Neither precedence, the trim/filter of empty entries, nor the try/catch fallback is exercised anywhere.
searchedFor: grep -n resolveCheckNames across repo (only fix-brief.mjs, fix-eligible.mjs, prior-findings.mjs)

samples.summary: The lens-stamping bug fix in main() is untested and untestable where it sits
samples.evidence: review-panel.mjs:2493 adds `.map((f) => ... typeof f.lens !== 'string' ? {...f, lens: lens.id} : f)` with a comment claiming it repairs a pre-existing bug that made the ENTIRE rebuttal/adjudication loop inert for re-found findings (findingSimilarity returns 0 unless `lens` matches — rounds.mjs:303). Nothing asserts it: grep of review-panel.test.mjs for `lens`-stamping/`typeof f.lens` finds nothing, and the two documented subtleties (stamp after clustering so `mergedAfter` identity removal still works; never overwrite an existing lens) have no coverage. Because the map is inline in `main()`, no test can reach it without extracting it — so a regression that reintroduces the inert-adjudication bug would ship silently.

samples.summary: The `--fix-reports` wiring in main() is not covered end to end
samples.evidence: review-panel.mjs:2191-2209 reads the fix-report file, calls `authorClaims`, merges `split.adjudicate` into `rebuttals` and routes `skipped`+`deferred` to `applySkipClaims`. review-panel.test.mjs has no test mentioning `fix-reports`, `authorClaims` or `skipClaims` (grep returned nothing); fix-report.test.mjs only tests `authorClaims` in isolation. The documented fail-quiet contract (missing/unparseable file → adjudicate none, never a failed panel) and the rebuttal-merge ordering are therefore unasserted, which is exactly the 'half-assembled and never fires' failure mode the fix-report tests themselves warn about.

samples.summary: applySkipClaims' `fixed` branch (deferred claims → 'unadjudicated-fix-claim') is never exercised
samples.evidence: applySkipClaims sets `verdict: c.status === 'fixed' ? 'unadjudicated-fix-claim' : 'skipped-by-author'`. main() feeds it `[...split.skipped, ...split.deferred]`, and deferred claims all have `status: 'fixed'` (fix-report.mjs authorClaims). The three tests in review-panel.test.mjs use status 'skipped' and a forged 'overturned' — both take the else branch — so the `fixed` verdict string and the guarantee that a capped fix-claim is UPHELD rather than credited is untested.
searchedFor: review-panel.test.mjs 'applySkipClaims' tests (3 cases, all non-'fixed' status)
fix-report.test.mjs deferred cap test (asserts split shape only, not applySkipClaims)

samples.summary: The 'matches a paraphrase' test uses byte-identical wording, so paraphrase matching is unverified
samples.evidence: `test("claimFor: matches a paraphrase of the finding in the same lens+file")` builds the claim with summary "null deref in parse()" and queries with the exact same string, so it only proves exact-text matching. The whole design rests on tolerating drift ('a paraphrase that drifts too far matches nothing' — the prompt in agent-fix.yml), and no test in fix-report.test.mjs feeds a genuinely reworded summary at or near DEFAULT_SIMILARITY=0.3. The test's own name asserts coverage that is not there.

samples.summary: The CLI halves of fix-eligible/fix-brief (exit codes, $GITHUB_OUTPUT emission) have no tests
samples.evidence: fix-eligible.mjs documents 'ALWAYS exits 0' for decisions and exit 2 for bad invocation, and agent-fix.yml's `Explain the refusal` step is built around exactly that split; `emit()` also formats `eligible/reason/head/failing` as k=v lines. fix-eligible.test.mjs only imports `classifyLensRuns`, `decideEligibility`, `readPrHead` — `emit`/`main` are not exported or spawned, so nothing checks the exit codes or the output-file format. Same for fix-brief.mjs's `main()` (exit 1 on no failing lenses, exit 2 on missing $GITHUB_OUTPUT) — fix-brief.test.mjs covers only the pure builders plus `ghOutputBlock`.
searchedFor: grep for spawn/execFile of these scripts in tests

samples.summary: cmdPost's round-trip guard and fail-open posting path are untested
samples.evidence: `cmdPost` (fix-report.mjs) is the only writer of reports: it warns on items missing lens/file/summary, refuses to post when `parseFixReportComment` cannot read the body back (exit 2), and deliberately exits 0 when `gh pr comment` fails. It is not exported and fix-report.test.mjs never invokes it (imports list ends at `readFixReports`), so none of those three behaviours — including the deliberate fail-open, which decides whether a fix job reds — has coverage.

samples.summary: cmdEffort (the new `metrics.mjs effort` subcommand) has no test
samples.evidence: metrics.test.mjs covers `renderFixEffort` and `classifyFixResult` well, but `cmdEffort` — which reads/parses the execution log, picks the LAST `type:'result'` message, always posts even with no log, and bails only on a post failure — is not exported and has no test. The 'last result message wins' selection and the 'always posts' guarantee are the parts the feature was asked for.

samples.summary: No test asserts that the branch checkout and agent steps are gated on eligibility
samples.evidence: checks.test.mjs's agent-fix tests assert step ORDER (trusted checkout < gate < brief < branch checkout), the trust gate, the re-verify step and the reporting steps — but nothing asserts the `if: steps.eligible.outputs.eligible == 'true'` guard that keeps an INELIGIBLE run from checking out the PR branch, installing deps and launching the fixer. That guard is the central precondition the whole workflow header is about, and it is one deleted line away from an ungated fixer with no test failing.
searchedFor: scripts/agent/checks.test.mjs agent-fix tests (routing, gate order, effort, trust, TOCTOU, refusal)

verdict.reason: resolveCheckNames is defined at scripts/agent/prior-findings.mjs:132 with a load-bearing contract (--checks precedence at 133-137, empty-list-on-unreadable-manifest at 139-144) and is the sole input resolver for fix-brief.mjs:34 and fix-eligible.mjs:37, where an empty result becomes exit 2 (fix-eligible.mjs:167,171-174). No test exercises it: repo-wide grep for resolveCheckNames/resolveNames yields only those three source files; prior-findings.test.mjs:3 imports only tagPriorFindings/lensCheckNames/collectPrior (lensCheckNames is tested at :84-89, the resolver is not); fix-eligible.test.mjs:3 imports only classifyLensRuns/decideEligibility/readPrHead and always passes a hard-coded NAMES array; fix-brief.test.mjs:3-14 imports only the pure builders. I also ruled out indirect coverage: no test file greps for '--checks', and the only CLIs run via execFileSync in tests are command.mjs, capture-meta.mjs, ai-prompt.mjs and git/novelty helpers — neither fix CLI is spawned. checks.test.mjs:252-354 only asserts on workflow YAML text ordering and never executes the scripts. So precedence, trim/filter and the try/catch fallback are wholly untested — a new behavior shipped with no meaningful test (major under the test-adequacy rubric).

finding.summary: The lens-stamping bug fix in main() is untested and untestable where it sits
finding.evidence: review-panel.mjs:2493 adds `.map((f) => ... typeof f.lens !== 'string' ? {...f, lens: lens.id} : f)` with a comment claiming it repairs a pre-existing bug that made the ENTIRE rebuttal/adjudication loop inert for re-found findings (findingSimilarity returns 0 unless `lens` matches — rounds.mjs:303). verdict.reason: The lens-stamping map at review-panel.mjs:2493 is genuinely new (absent from .trusted/scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs) and genuinely untested. It is the sole stamping site in the file (a grep for f.lens/lensId/lens: lens.id shows lens otherwise only flowing into session logMeta at 1650 and the priorForLens filter at 2448), it is inline in main() and not exported, and no test drives main() (no child_process/spawnSync in review-panel.test.mjs). I also checked the repo's own convention for pinning main()-inline logic — source-regex tests at review-panel.test.mjs:578/598/605/713/728/738/1347/1704/3017 — and none of them assert the stamp. The nearest one (review-panel.test.mjs:1346-1409) deliberately anchors on the bare binding `const merged =` (1403-1406) and its comment explicitly says it does not care which functions produce the value, so it passes with or without the `.map`. Neither documented subtlety (stamp after clustering so mergedAfter's identity-based removal still works; never overwrite an existing lens) has any coverage. Searched wider in rebuttal.test.mjs, finding-match.test.mjs, prior-findings.test.mjs, rounds.test.mjs, fix-report.test.mjs and harvest.test.mjs: every `lens:` there is a hand-built fixture that already carries a lens, and finding-match.test.mjs:125/152-159 tests the findingSimilarity lens gate (the consumer) rather than the stamp. A behavior change on the field the entire rebuttal/adjudication match keys on, with no meaningful test, is major under the missing-tests limb of the test-adequacy rubric.
